title: Retro Arcade: Snake
story: The year is 1997. You're holding a Nokia 3310. A black pixel snake slithers across a green screen, eating dots of food, growing longer with every bite. You dodge the walls. You dodge yourself. It's the most addictive game ever written in 500 lines of assembly. Today, you write the entire engine in XIOM — the snake, the food, the grid, the collision detection. Your snake moves, eats, grows, and dies. You just built a real game loop from scratch. This is the most complex program in the entire curriculum. And you did it.
why: Snake synthesizes every concept: Vec for the snake body, structs for game state, enums for direction, random for food placement, grid collision detection, game loop architecture with update/render cycle, and scoring — a complete real-time game engine.
analogy: A remote-controlled caterpillar on a checkered floor. The caterpillar's head follows your joystick (direction), and its body segments follow the head exactly — each segment moves into the space the previous segment just left. Food dots appear randomly on the floor; eating one makes the caterpillar grow one segment longer. Crash into a wall or your own body, and the game resets. Your code IS the caterpillar's brain and the floor's physics.
try_it: Add a score display that prints after each render. Add speed levels: Easy (slow), Medium, Hard (fast). Add WASD-style input simulation by reading from a hardcoded Vec of directions. When the snake eats food, grow by one segment (don't remove the tail on that frame). Add a 'play again' loop. Add wall-wrapping mode where the snake teleports to the opposite side.
tips: Snake movement: insert new head at front, remove tail (pop last) — unless food was eaten, then keep tail
Render head as 'O' and body segments as 'o' — visually distinguishes the snake's direction
Collision: check walls first (fast), then iterate body[1..] for self-collision
common_mistakes: Checking self-collision starting at index 0 — the head is always at its own position, so start at 1
Not removing the tail when moving without food — snake would grow forever
Food spawning on top of the snake body — must regenerate if the random point overlaps any segment
